title: On Asking the old man about the road
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：ask　|　正文 347 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 ask 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 the porter ① asked the old man about the road in public, and every visitor in the coast said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the porter ② asks the old man about the road in silence without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ ask the old man about the road at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ asked the old man about the road before — a line in the journal for August 1955 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Asking the old man about the road in public, the porter said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the bag at the far cove, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ ask for a straight answer in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Ask for a straight answer at once and never mention it again.

By 1968 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the journal, and a new visitor from the next coast ⑧ asks for a straight answer in public every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the cove, said nothing at all; she simply  asked the old man about the road again when nobody else would.

To ask the old man about the road, my mother said in 1973, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the coast remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the coast forgets, somebody asks the old man about the road in silence again and somebody must ask the old man about the road in public all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 询问（一般过去式 asked the old man about the road：1961 年挑夫头一回这样做，当着众人面）
B. v. 询问（一般现在 asks the old man about the road：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 询问（不定式 to ask the old man about the road：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 询问（过去完成时 had asked the old man about the road：1955 年八月的行记上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 询问（动名词 asking the old man about the road 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 要求（ask for a straight answer：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去要求要一句痛快的回答）
G. v. 要求（ask for a straight answer：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 询问（后段两处：新来的游客照例 asks for a straight answer，而母亲又一次 asked the old man about the road）

items.q: asked the old man about the road
asks the old man about the road
to ask the old man about the road
asked the old man about the road before
asking the old man about the road
ask for a straight answer in silence
ask for a straight answer at once
asks for a straight answer in public

answers.why: ask 意为“询问”，1961 年挑夫当着众人面询问向老人打听那条路，那是海岸里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 asked。
ask 意为“询问”，自那以后挑夫一言不发地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 asks。
ask 意为“询问”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯询问向老人打听那条路”，此处为不定式 to ask the old man about the road。
ask 意为“询问”，行记里 八月 那行字说明早在 1968 年之前就有人询问过，故用过去完成时 had asked。
ask 意为“询问”，挑夫说“询问向老人打听那条路这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 asking the old man about the road 作主语。
ask 意为“要求”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去要求要一句痛快的回答”，should ever 之后用原形 ask for a straight answer。
ask 意为“要求”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻要求要一句痛快的回答（ask for a straight answer at once），以后再也不要提起。
ask 意为“询问”，新来的游客每个星期都照例要求要一句痛快的回答，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 asks。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1961 年，挑夫当着众人面询问向老人打听那条路；海岸里每一个游客都说这是头一回。（asked the old man about the road）
多年以后，挑夫仍一言不发地做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（asks the old man about the road）
母亲后来说，难就难在肯询问向老人打听那条路这件事本身。（to ask the old man about the road）
早在 1955 年就有人询问向老人打听那条路，八月那天行记上的一行字就是证据。（had asked the old man about the road）
挑夫说过，当着众人面询问向老人打听那条路这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（asking the old man about the road 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻要求要一句痛快的回答，以后再也不要提起。（ask for a straight answer，祈使句）
answers: In 1961 the porter asked the old man about the road in public, and every visitor in the coast said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there.
Three weeks on, the porter still asks the old man about the road in silence without being asked.
My mother said later that to ask the old man about the road at all was the part nobody had expected.
Somebody had asked the old man about the road long before 1968, and the line in the journal for August proves it.
Asking the old man about the road in public, the porter said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
The rule the old hands handed down was plain: Ask for a straight answer at once and never mention it again.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 ask 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1961 the porter asked the old man about the road in public, and nobody in the coast forgot it.
Even now the porter asks the old man about the road in silence whenever the coast asks.
Asking the old man about the road in public, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever ask for a straight answer in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new visitor from the next coast asks for a straight answer in public every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother asked the old man about the road again, and the coast remembered that half.
